name: Execution Admissibility Ontology (EAO)
license: Text © JExec. Cite with attribution and a link to the canonical URL.
definition: A classification of the ways an intended execution fails to be admissible before it mutates state.

classes.name: Unstated Intent
classes.summary: The execution never declares what it is trying to do, so admissibility cannot even be evaluated.

defaultConsequences.condition: intent declared but too vague to evaluate

classes.name: Unattributed Actor
classes.summary: There is no verified answer to the question: who or what is executing this?

classes.name: Unverified Authority
classes.summary: Authority is claimed, but never verified against an identifiable source.

classes.name: Authority–Scope Mismatch
classes.summary: Verified authority exists — for a different scope than the one this execution mutates.

defaultConsequences.condition: authority explicitly does not cover the declared scope

classes.name: Unbounded Scope
classes.summary: The execution cannot state its blast radius before it runs.

defaultConsequences.condition: unbounded elsewhere, or partially bounded in production

classes.name: Missing Evidence
classes.summary: Nothing supports that this execution should happen — no tests, no approval reference, no provenance, no policy match.

defaultConsequences.condition: evidence missing for an irreversible or unclassified mutation
evidence missing for a reversible mutation

classes.name: Stale Evidence
classes.summary: Evidence exists — but it describes a system, artifact, or moment that no longer exists.

defaultConsequences.condition: stale evidence behind an irreversible mutation
stale evidence behind a reversible mutation

classes.name: Unclassified Risk
classes.summary: Nobody has said what this execution can change or damage.

defaultConsequences.condition: risk unclassified — and treated as irreversible by every evidence rule until classified

classes.name: Irreversibility Blindness
classes.summary: An irreversible mutation is handled with the same casualness as a reversible one.

defaultConsequences.condition: irreversible mutation with no declared reversal or review path

classes.name: Unrecorded Decision
classes.summary: The execution may even be admissible — but no durable record of that decision will exist.

defaultConsequences.condition: no admissibility record produced or stored
